【原视频简介】
One coconut can become two completely different foods.

The clear liquid inside can become chewy nata de coco, while the white coconut meat can become rich coconut milk and eventually coconut candy.

But these two products are created through almost opposite manufacturing processes.

Inside the factory, mature coconuts are opened and separated into distinct material streams.

Coconut water is filtered and prepared as a fermentation medium. Cellulose-producing bacteria gradually build a thick bacterial-cellulose layer at the liquid-air surface. The resulting nata de coco is washed, conditioned, cut into cubes, sweetened, heat-treated, and packed.

The coconut meat follows a completely different route.

The white kernel is cleaned, grated, and mechanically pressed to extract coconut milk or cream. Sugar and malt syrup are added before the mixture is heated and continuously stirred.

As water evaporates, the liquid becomes increasingly concentrated until it reaches the thick, chewy consistency needed for coconut candy.

The hot candy mass is formed, cooled, cut into individual pieces, and wrapped for sale.

This factory process reveals two very different food-science transformations hidden inside a single coconut:

Clear coconut water becomes a solid bacterial-cellulose jelly through fermentation.

Solid coconut meat becomes a liquid coconut-milk emulsion before heat and water removal turn it into chewy candy.
